curriculum: The standard Utrecht Spanish Language and Culture degree totals 180 EC. Article 3.5 and Annexes 1–2 establish a 127.5 EC major: 67.5 EC of compulsory courses, 7.5 EC for the Spanish-language thesis, 45 EC of advanced courses and one 7.5 EC methods course. Annex 3 establishes 52.5 EC of profiling, including a 30 EC coherent package. A Utrecht minor qualifies; an external minor, study abroad or a specially assembled package needs advance approval. The Crossing Borders depth package may also serve as profiling in this track. The Crossing Borders track has a different major and profiling division. The prospectus describes subject matter and provides learning context; the OER and start-year guide control the selected requirements. The degree is mainly in Spanish with some English courses under Article 3.3. The 0 EC basic grammar test is required, and the programme outcomes include at least B2 speaking and writing and C1 listening and reading.
progression: The illustrated Year 1 follows the two required base packages and the A1 to B2 Spanish acquisition sequence alongside literary studies, comparative morphosyntax, theater and film, and sociolinguistics. In 2027–2028, the odd rotation places literacy and cultural awareness, Migration and Diaspora, Testimonios, crónicas, representaciones, and Variation and Change in Language in successive blocks. Formal titles and credit values control; the prospectus currently uses imágenes in its title for the testimony and chronicles course. The four odd-year catalog codes were pending in the OER. The chosen level-3 intercultural communication methods course fits block 3 alongside that block’s depth course. Profiling fills the remaining 22.5 EC in Year 2. In 2028–2029, the first two advanced courses in the even rotation fit blocks 1 and 2. The writing workshop and thesis run in blocks 3 and 4 respectively in the cohort guide. The six depth courses, methods, writing and thesis yield 67.5 EC at level 3, above the 45 EC minimum. The 30 EC coherent package fills the remaining Year 3 load.
components: First course in the Spanish language sequence, working toward CEFR A1.
Introduces methods for interpreting literary texts.
Second course in the Spanish language sequence, working toward CEFR A2.
Compares how languages form words and sentences.
Third course in the Spanish language sequence, working toward CEFR B1.
Teatro, cine e intermedialidad: España y América Latina
Studies theater and cinema in Spain and Latin America and how they interact with other media.
Fourth course in the Spanish language sequence, working toward CEFR B2.
Studies Spanish in its social contexts in Spain and Latin America.
Competencias de lectura y conciencia cultural: España y América Latina
Develops reading skills and cultural awareness through material from Spain and Latin America.
Studies migration and diaspora in the Transatlantic Perspectives package.
Testimonios, crónicas, representaciones: España y América Latina
Studies testimonies, chronicles and representation in Spain and Latin America.
Examines how language varies and changes.
An approved research methods choice focused on intercultural communication.
Electives beyond the 30 EC package, subject to Utrecht’s degree rules.
Lengua, cultura e identidad: España y América Latina
One of two additional advanced courses. It examines language, culture and identity in Spain and Latin America.
One of two additional advanced courses. It examines contested interpretations of the past.
Taller de escritura profesional, creativa y académica
Develops professional, creative and academic writing in Spanish and prepares students for the thesis.
Students carry out an independent research project and write the thesis in Spanish.
A coherent elective package, such as a minor or approved study abroad.
